response.rationale: R5 is the most complete: it uniquely combines obstruction-specific raw signs (dilated jejunum with spring sign, active gas-through-water sound) with dense tubular shadows, pneumatosis, and thickened wall. R3/R4 capture free gas and pneumatosis but miss the obstruction-specific signs; R1 has nonspecific CT/lab findings; R2 has no raw-vignette support. Free gas is a competing sign but can be a complication of obstruction/ischemia, and active bowel sounds with no muscle tension favor obstruction.

rejected.why: Bilious vomiting, free gas, and pneumatosis are nonspecific for a fistula and no obstruction-specific raw signs are cited.
Thickened wall, dense tubular shadows, and CRP are nonspecific and can be secondary to obstruction; lacks dilated jejunum and active bowel sounds.
No raw-vignette support spans are supplied; only generator assessments, which are non-raw opinions and cannot serve as evidence.
